feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced. The candidate is iteration 1, the best raced design (52.8), with one change: controller.ki goes from 0 to 0.4. Geometry (x = +/-0.03, 16 mm footprints), kp 1.5, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4 and line_loss last_direction are unchanged. Iteration 1 went off track on all 60 trials with one line-loss event each, rms_error about 0.03 m and max_error 0.061 to 0.065 m. The iteration 3 rationale links that pattern to a fixed left/right motor bias, which proportional-only control cannot remove. That hypothesis is plausible, since rms_error is steady across tracks, but it is not yet confirmed. The candidate is valid, differs from the best raced design by one controlled variable, and the race is the only way to test the bias hypothesis, so racing is worth more than another revision round.

Risk to watch: integral action on the s-bend and slalom can wind up while the signal stays one-sided through a bend, which could push the robot off the line on the bend itself. The integral is clamped at +/-2, so the worst case is about 0.8 of turn (about 280 PWM), which is bounded but not negligible.

What to change after the race, depending on its telemetry. (a) If rms_error falls below about 0.025 m and max_error drops below 0.06 m with line_loss_events at 0 or 1, keep ki 0.4 and test base_speed 1.6 next for completion time. (b) If rms_error and max_error are essentially unchanged, the bias hypothesis is wrong, so revert ki to 0 and test kd 0.15 as a single change. (c) If max_error rises or the s-bend or slalom worsens while rms_error improves, integral windup is the likely cause; reduce ki to 0.15 to 0.2 before raising speed. (d) If progress stays low with no line loss, base_speed is the limit, so test 1.6 with the best ki.
requested_changes: After this race, if rms_error falls below about 0.025 m with max_error below 0.06 m and line_loss_events at 0 or 1, keep controller.ki = 0.4 and test controller.base_speed = 1.6 to reduce completion_time.

If rms_error and max_error are unchanged from iteration 1 (rms about 0.03 m, max about 0.061 to 0.065 m), set controller.ki back to 0 and test controller.kd = 0.15 as a single change, since iteration 1 showed damping as the next variable.
If max_error worsens on the s-bend or slalom while rms_error improves, reduce controller.ki to 0.15 to 0.2 to limit integral windup on one-sided bends before any speed change.
